title: 返事を待つポスター
paragraphs: The drama club needed a poster for its next play. Two students, Lily and Dan, offered to design it. Lily worked quickly and sent a finished poster that evening. Dan said he wanted to ask the actors about the story first. When Lily saw no reply from him the following morning, she thought he had forgotten the task. She told the club leader that she might have to do everything alone. Later that day, Dan arrived with notes from three actors and several small drawings. He had spent the evening talking to them and had planned to show his ideas at the meeting. Lily realized that she had misunderstood his silence. This made her feel embarrassed. The two students agreed to send short progress messages each evening, even when their work was not ready to show. They combined Lily's clear lettering with Dan's picture of the main character. Their final poster was better because both kinds of work had been included.

title: 二種類の展示札
paragraphs: At a school exhibition, the science class showed models of bridges. Each model had a long card explaining its design. Younger visitors often looked at the model for a few seconds and walked away without reading. The students wanted to help these visitors understand what made each bridge different. They added short cards with a question at the top, such as Which bridge can carry the most toy cars? Below each question was a simple action that visitors could try. These were placed in front of the longer explanations. Children began testing the models, then asked to read more about the strongest designs. The students kept both kinds of card because some adults wanted detailed information from the start. At the end of the day, the class discussed what had changed. They had not made the science easier by removing important ideas. Instead, they had created a first step that gave visitors a reason to explore those ideas for themselves.

title: 借りた傘の行方
paragraphs: On a rainy afternoon, the library put a basket of spare umbrellas near its entrance. Visitors could borrow one and return it on another day. For the first week, almost none came back. The librarian, Ken, did not want to end the service immediately. He asked several visitors whether the return instructions were clear. One visitor said she had borrowed an umbrella but could not remember which building it belonged to. Another thought she had to return it before the library closed that same evening. Ken attached a bright label to each handle. It showed the library's name and said that umbrellas could be returned any day the library was open. He also put an empty return basket inside the door. They made the service easier to use, and more umbrellas came back the next week. Ken learned that people could want to do the right thing but still need clear information about how to do it.

title: キャンプ場からのメール
paragraphs: Dear members, Thank you for joining next month's weekend camp. Please read this message before packing your bags. We will meet at the east entrance of the station at eight on Saturday morning. The west entrance is closer to the shops, but our bus cannot stop there. It will leave at eight fifteen, so please call the leader if you are delayed. Bring a packed lunch for the first day. We will cook dinner together, and breakfast will be provided on Sunday. You do not need to bring a cooking pot because the campsite lends them to groups. You should bring your own cup and a small towel. The weather in the hills can change quickly. Even if the morning is sunny, keep a rain jacket in your bag. We have planned outdoor games and a short nature walk. If heavy rain makes those activities impossible, we will use the meeting hall for a map game and a craft session. Best wishes, The camp team.

会員の皆様、来月の週末キャンプへの参加ありがとうございます。荷造り前にお読みください。土曜八時に駅東口集合です。店に近い西口にはバスが停車できません。八時十五分発なので遅れる場合はリーダーへ電話を。初日の昼食は持参し、夕食は皆で作り日曜朝食は提供します。鍋はキャンプ場が貸すので不要ですがカップと小さなタオルは持参してください。山の天候は変わりやすいので朝晴れていても雨具を。屋外ゲームと自然散歩を予定し、大雨なら集会所で地図ゲームと工作を行います。キャンプ係より。

title: 二台の録音機
paragraphs: For a local history event, Isabel interviewed her grandfather about the old railway. She brought a small digital recorder and her phone. The recorder had a new battery, while the phone was nearly out of power. Her grandfather spoke for an hour about trains that carried fruit from nearby farms. Isabel listened carefully and asked about the workers at the station. Before leaving, she checked both devices. The phone had stopped after ten minutes, but the other had recorded the whole conversation. She was glad that she had not depended on only one device. At home, she copied the recording to her computer and wrote down the parts she wanted to use. Her grandfather later helped her check the names of people and places. At the event, visitors heard short sections of his voice beside old photographs. Several said that hearing someone who had actually worked there made the railway seem more real than a list of dates alone.

title: 一番前の席
paragraphs: At the town theater, a student named Owen helped visitors find their seats. He liked working near the front because he could see the stage clearly before each show. One evening, a woman asked whether she could exchange her front seat for one farther back. Owen was surprised. He thought everyone would prefer the closest possible view. The woman explained that her young son enjoyed seeing the whole stage at once. From the front, he had to turn his head often and sometimes missed what happened on the other side. Owen asked the ticket manager, who found two empty seats near the middle. Those gave the family the view they wanted. After the show, the boy described a scene with dancers on both sides of the stage. Owen understood why the change had mattered. When helping later visitors, he began asking what kind of view they wanted instead of assuming that his own favorite seats would be best for everyone.

title: 朝の観察記録
paragraphs: Grace's class planted beans in small pots beside the classroom window. Each pair measured a plant every morning. Grace and her partner used different rulers, so their numbers sometimes seemed strange. On Monday, Grace wrote that the plant was twelve centimeters tall. On Tuesday, her partner measured eleven. They first thought the plant had become shorter overnight. Their teacher asked them to show how they measured it. Grace started from the surface of the soil, but her partner started from the bottom of the pot. They also placed the ruler at different angles. This explained why their records could not be compared fairly. The pair agreed to measure from the soil surface with the ruler standing straight. They wrote the method at the top of their record sheet and took a photograph each Friday. Their later numbers showed a steady increase. The lesson was not only about growing beans; it also showed why people need to describe their methods when sharing measurements.

クラスで窓辺に豆を植え、ペアで毎朝測った。グレースは月曜に十二センチ、相方は火曜に十一センチと記し縮んだと思った。先生に測り方を示すと、彼女は土の表面、相方は鉢の底を起点にし角度も違った。そのため公平に比べられなかった。二人は土から垂直に測ると統一して用紙上部に方法を書き、金曜には写真も撮った。以後は安定した増加を示した。豆を育てるだけでなく、測定結果を共有する際に方法の説明が必要な理由を学んだ。

title: 返信の小さな工夫
paragraphs: Dear Yuna, I am happy that you will visit our school next month. You asked what to bring for the art exchange. Please bring three photographs of places that matter to you. They do not have to show famous buildings. A street, a park bench, or a room at home can be interesting if you can explain its importance. We will use the pictures to make a shared wall display. Each visitor will work with a student from our school. We have paper, paint, and glue, so you can leave those at home. Please tell us if you want to use any other materials. On the first afternoon, we will visit the town gallery. It is a short walk from school, but comfortable shoes will help. I have attached a map and a timetable. If anything is unclear, write back with your questions. We want you to feel ready, and we are looking forward to learning about your town through your eyes. Best, Eva.

title: 砂浜に残すもの
paragraphs: A beach club organized a drawing day for children. The plan was to make large pictures in the sand and take photographs before the sea covered them. Some parents suggested painting on stones instead because the pictures in the sand would disappear. The organizer, Rosa, said that disappearing was part of the activity. Children could try a shape, change it, and start again without worrying about keeping the result forever. On the day, groups drew boats, fish, and imaginary islands. A boy named Leo spent a long time making a road between two islands. When the first small wave reached it, he looked disappointed. Then he watched the water make a new curve in the road and smiled. He added another line to match it. Rosa photographed the changing picture, not just its final form. Later, Leo said the best part had been watching his design work with the sea. His drawing was gone, but he remembered the experience clearly.

海辺のクラブは砂に大きな絵を描き、波が覆う前に撮影する会を計画した。消えない石の絵を提案した親もいたが、主催者ローザは消えることも活動の一部で、永久保存を気にせず試し直せると説明した。当日は船、魚、想像の島を描いた。レオは島を結ぶ道を時間をかけて作り、最初の波で残念そうにしたが、水が道に新しい曲線を作るのを見て笑い、それに合わせ線を加えた。ローザは最終形だけでなく変化も撮った。彼は海と一緒に作る過程が一番よかったと話した。絵は消えても体験は鮮明に残った。

title: 交換日記の白いページ
paragraphs: When Max moved to another town, he and his cousin decided to send a notebook between their homes. Each person would write for a week and then post it. They hoped to keep sharing small parts of their daily lives. At first, Max filled every page with long reports about school. His cousin, however, sent back drawings, ticket pieces, and only a few sentences. Max wondered whether his cousin was less interested in the project. Then one page contained a drawing of the street where they had played together as children. It brought back a memory that Max had never written about. He realized that the drawings were another way of continuing their conversation. In his next turn, he left a blank page and asked his cousin to add a picture of a favorite place. The notebook gradually became a mixture of words and images. Neither cousin had to copy the other's style for their shared project to feel equally important to both of them.
転居したマックスといとこはノートを一週ずつ書いて郵送し日常を共有した。彼は学校の長い報告、相手は絵や切符と短い文だったので、関心が薄いのかと思った。だが幼い頃遊んだ通りの絵で、自分が書かなかった記憶がよみがえった。絵も会話の続け方と気づき、次は白紙を残して好きな場所を描いてと頼んだ。ノートは徐々に言葉と画像の混合になった。同じ書き方をまねなくても、共同の試みは二人に等しく大切でありえた。
